record.paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
record.context_brief: deconfinement and hydrodynamic expansion in high-multiplicity pp
record.original_question: In very high-energy proton-proton collisions with low impact parameter and high charged-particle multiplicity, do multiparton interactions and rescatterings transfer enough energy into a proton-sized volume to create a close-to-equilibrium deconfined initial state, allow thermalization despite the small system size, and produce a proton-sized fireball that expands hydrodynamically or collectively?

evidence.quote: Such multiparton interactions and rescatterings could contribute to a large energy transfer in a collision volume of proton size, easily reaching the deconﬁnement conditions. If this is the case and considering that the mean free path of the constituents in a deconﬁned medium is of the order of 0.2 - 0.3 fm, a close to equilibrium deconﬁned initial state could be expected in very high energy pp collisions. Therefore, quite probable at such energies, a piece of matter of proton size, with a radius of few times larger than the mean free path, expands hydrodynamically once the energy transfer is signiﬁcantly large, i.e. low impact parameter - high charged particle multiplicity.

The energy density easily reaches the deconﬁnement value and considering the mean free path of the constituents of the deconﬁned phase, thermalization cannot be excluded. If this is the case, such an initial state, thermalized and of extremely high energy density, will follow a collective type expansion [25, 26, 27, 28] which can be evidenced experimentally by analyzing the same observables as the ones presented above for A-A collisions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider proton-proton (pp) collisions at very high center-of-mass energies (of order several TeV), restricted to events with low impact parameter and unusually high charged-particle multiplicity. Model the collision as producing, within a region of roughly proton size (radius R of order 1 fm), a system of partonic constituents whose multiparton interactions and subsequent rescatterings deposit energy into this volume. Assume that in a deconfined QCD medium the mean free path of the constituents is λ ≈ 0.2–0.3 fm, so that R/λ is of order a few.

Address the following physics question precisely: do the multiparton interactions and rescatterings in such high-multiplicity, low-impact-parameter pp events transfer enough energy density into the proton-sized volume to (i) exceed the QCD deconfinement threshold and produce a close-to-equilibrium deconfined initial state, (ii) allow approximate local thermalization despite the smallness of the system relative to typical heavy-ion fireballs, and (iii) produce a proton-sized fireball that subsequently undergoes hydrodynamic or otherwise collective expansion, observable through the same flow-type observables (e.g. long-range azimuthal correlations, radial and anisotropic flow harmonics, mass-ordering of mean transverse momenta, identified-hadron spectra) used to characterize collectivity in nucleus-nucleus collisions?

Provide a quantitative theoretical and/or experimental determination of whether each of (i), (ii), and (iii) holds for high-multiplicity pp collisions at LHC-class energies.
artifact.category_tag: QGP and collectivity in small systems
artifact.status_search_result: Experimental observations at the LHC (long-range "ridge" correlations, mass-ordered radial flow, strangeness enhancement, nonzero v_n in high-multiplicity pp) have established clear collectivity-like signatures in high-multiplicity pp events, and hydrodynamic models reproduce many features, suggesting QGP-like behavior. However, whether a true close-to-equilibrium deconfined and thermalized state is formed in pp—as opposed to initial-state (e.g. CGC/color-domain) origins of collectivity—remains under active debate as of 2024–2025 reviews. The question is therefore partially resolved on the phenomenological side but not fully settled theoretically.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Hot QCD Matter 2024 – Bulk Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Advances in theoretical frameworks, including hydrodynamics... refine our knowledge of the thermodynamic properties of strongly interacting matter.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; bulk properties and thermalization in small systems still under refinement.

status_evidence.title: Probing QGP-like Dynamics via Multi-Strange Hadron Production in High-Multiplicity pp Collisions
status_evidence.snippet: effective temperature decreased with multiplicity, signaling the transition from a thermalized QGP-like state (high multiplicity) to a fragmented, non-equilibrium system
status_evidence.claim: Recent measurements support QGP-like thermalized behavior at high multiplicity in pp.

status_evidence.title: Collective flow from AA, pA to pp collisions – Toward a unified paradigm
status_evidence.snippet: unified paradigm in describing the observed collectivity across all hadronic collision systems is emerging
status_evidence.claim: Collectivity in pp is established phenomenologically; theoretical interpretation (hydro vs initial-state) still debated.

status_evidence.title: Smallest drop of QGP: Thermodynamic properties
status_evidence.snippet: Smallest drop of QGP: Thermodynamic properties of collisions
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2024 work characterizing whether smallest systems form a QGP drop.
